# Tetorica SPU Synth

PlayStation 1 SPU synthesizer / emulator

Serve this directory over HTTPS or localhost and open index.html. AudioWorklet requires a secure context; opening files directly is unsupported. For itch.io, upload the ZIP as an HTML project and select index.html. Enable audio and use the keyboard. All 24 round-robin voices share one instrument. An optional wide software accumulator provides 12 dB mixing headroom, with compensating output gain. Voice registers retain their original precision; compensated dry single-note PCM matches the legacy mixer without the extra rounding noise of reducing voice volume registers. Extreme sums can still reach the original SPU saturation limit. Use the PCM, ADSR, FX, Audio and PSF / VAB tabs to draw a short waveform, edit its envelope, add reverb or load a recording. The PSF / VAB tab opens standard Sony VAB v6/v7 or matching VH + VB files, and statically extracts contiguous VAB banks and uniquely matched separated VH / VB from PSF1/MiniPSF sets with their PSFLib dependencies. Split bodies require full coverage and exact sample / END boundaries; ambiguous candidates are rejected. Split pairing is inferred from sample structure rather than original driver transfers; the bank label shows matched VB and the instrument should be compared with its source song. After opening a PSF folder or file set, the PSF song list and playback controls appear above Envelope / Waveform / Spectrum, showing the folder and relative song paths. Related PSFLib files remain dependencies. Choose a song above the monitor and Extract VAB beside Play / Pause / Stop; this opens the PSF / VAB Bank / Tone list. Select a bank and Tone, then Load selected Tone to audition it, Save selected Tone to preset to store a one-Tone standard VAB and supplemental JSON, or Save bank to presets to keep the full original VAB plus each available Tone as JSON in Files / presets. Full export retains original header, attributes, body prefix, sample padding and unavailable Tones; matching VH+VB become one combined VAB. Selected export preserves the original Program ID and raw attributes/sample, renumbering Tone to 0 and Sample to 1. No ADPCM is re-encoded. These direct saves need no audio context, keep the current edited sound, held notes, Code and PSF playback / Pause position, and do not load SPU RAM. The Preset selector beside Instrument name lists standard VAB Program/Tone choices and supplemental JSON separately, follows Files changes and restoration, and keeps Keyboard / Code mode. VAB choices work directly without JSON; volume/pan use the existing approximation and reverb send uses current Synth shared reverb. JSON retains original ADPCM, loop, ADSR, tuning, approximate volumes/pan/send and the shared reverb settings at save time (Off before audio starts), with PMON, Noise and Morph disabled. Unavailable Tones are skipped only in JSON with reasons; names never overwrite existing files. VAB+JSON must fit the 16 MiB project or nothing is added. Export the saved VAB from Files to reuse it outside Tetorica. The reusable browser module synth-spu/spu_synth_vab.js exports readVab, prepareVabTone and exportVab; load prepared ADPCM with the normal SPU loadADPCM/setPreset API, without Tetorica JSON. The VAB parser is not yet an npm export. Library-only sets are labelled Library and support extraction with song playback disabled. Extract ZIP archives first. Unavailable Tones show a reason, an available count and an expandable reason list. A single loop-start marker in a one-shot sample is accepted without rewriting its ADPCM bytes; the END Repeat flag controls looping. The selected PSF1 / MiniPSF can also Play song, Pause / Resume and Stop song using a separate Play! CPU / HLE machine with the same fixed MAME-derived SPU DSP as the Synth. No external BIOS is needed. Song ADPCM, Gaussian interpolation, ADSR, Noise, PMON, main / reverb output volumes and shared reverb use that DSP, with hardware mixing and no keyboard software click guard. CPU execution remains HLE with basic-block timing, not cycle-exact PS1 emulation. Unsupported volume sweeps, 8-byte-only voice addresses and transfer modes fail explicitly. The existing keyboard SPU is unchanged. Your edited instrument is kept. While playing, selected PSF CH Volume, PITCH, ADSR and keys share the original machine. Later CPU writes take ownership; an old key release or Pitch reset cannot stop or retune their replacement. Commands apply to the next unrendered boundary while retaining about 0.2 seconds of lookahead. Sample RAM, Start/Repeat and shared effects stay read-only in PSF CH view. Synth view edits the separate author bank while the PSF continues. While paused in PSF CH view with Live On, keyboard keys temporarily audition the selected ADPCM at Reference key tuning or Noise at its shared Clock; the PSF position and frozen CH view stay in place. In Synth view, including with Live Off, keys play the edited instrument while preserving Pause. Switching channel/reference, Resume, Stop, Capture or Code retires the temporary audition and restores the latest edited instrument bank. In paused Synth view, PCM, ADSR, Reverb, Morph, Noise and PMON edits keep the original song position and frozen CH state. Switch to a PSF CH to compare the source, then back to Synth to continue with the latest edits. Loading another preset, VAB Tone or audio sample, Reset instrument, running Code or an explicit Stop still stops the song. Master and monitor share the existing audio bus, with no extra SPU or AudioContext. The seek bar commits on release or arrow-key release. A separate candidate PSF machine silently renders from the beginning to the requested frame, discarding early PCM without scheduling audio or retaining long PCM/Live/RAM history. The previous machine and unplayed buffers are kept until success. Pause seeks stay paused; playing seeks continue playback; stopped-entry seeks prepare a paused position. Cancel seek or Escape returns to the previous position/state; failure keeps it too, while Stop/source changes invalidate candidates. Only one candidate is prepared at a time. Target positions are initially limited to 30 minutes and processing to 30 seconds, checked between small native render slices; a slice itself cannot be interrupted. The UI shows progress and blocks keyboard/Capture/edits until arrival. length + fade tags provide only a reference range without automatic end/fade. Unknown duration shows ? with an expanding five-minute range. Selected CH/Dry/view and the edited Synth instrument are kept, and Live/Capture use the arrival frame. No seek checkpoint cache is retained. PSF2, ambiguous or padded split VH / VB layouts, custom and runtime-packed banks are unsupported. Audio accepts up to 32 MiB and 30 minutes. Recordings beyond free SPU RAM automatically use Software audio: shared signed mono PCM in host memory, with SPU Gaussian interpolation, pitch, ADSR, PMON and reverb. This is a software extension beyond PS1 hardware RAM. Long audio is included in version 2 presets. FX also includes Pitch Modulation: a silent Sine, Triangle, Saw or Square source per note, Ratio, Depth and approximate Decay (zero holds). PMON uses 12 pairs of voices; switching On or Off stops current notes. The PCM tab also offers SPU Noise with a shared clock and per-note ADSR; keys trigger envelopes rather than noise pitch. Noise and PMON switch each other off. Changing the sound source stops current notes and keeps the original PCM/audio sample. Software morph in the PCM tab blends two 112-sample cycles (shapes or captured current PCM) with a live A/B slider. This is a Tetorica software feature, not a built-in PS1 SPU effect: the software writes a blended ADPCM cycle into SPU sample memory without retriggering notes. When enabled, Wave A, Wave B and the blended result overlay one canvas in distinct colors. Select A or B to draw that endpoint directly on the same canvas or edit its numeric samples. Disabling keeps the last blend; loading audio disables Morph. Settings are included in presets. The upper Envelope, Waveform and Spectrum views display live output, with Pitch and a second synchronized Morph slider beside the display. Morph holds its value when released; enable it in the PCM tab. The Keyboard / Code tabs share this same SPU and current instrument. Code uses await useSoundChip("ps1") with explicit physical channels, liveLoop, livePrepare, tween and host software liveFx. Save to presets beside Instrument name and Save sound in Files add /presets/<instrument name>.spu.json, including the sample and settings. Existing files are kept with a numbered suffix for duplicate names. Saving opens Files without changing Keyboard / Code mode, editor focus or the current performance. Selecting a saved sound JSON restores it and prepares its text in the shared Code editor. File selection keeps Keyboard / Code mode; choose Code to see or edit the selected text. JSON and other text edits save locally without applying the sound; select the sound JSON again to apply changes. Run / Apply are enabled only for JavaScript files. Right-click Files for Duplicate, Rename, Delete, New instrument, New JavaScript file or New folder (also Context Menu key / Shift+F10). Duplicate uses a free -copy name and keeps nested data and empty folders without loading a sound or stopping a performance. New instrument saves the current edited sound to the chosen .spu.json path. Opening the menu never applies or plays a sound. Escape or an outside click dismisses it. Opening or extracting a bank does not automatically save all Tones. Files retains code, modules, opaque data and portable SPU sound presets; importing or restoring a project never runs code or starts audio. The shared Live view observes the selected physical CH1-24 from PSF playback or Code without replacing the authored instrument. PSF Live is on by default, can be disabled, and uses bounded snapshots at or before the audible position. Selected CH only - Dry is a Tetorica software listening helper, initially Off. It listens to the selected dry channel while all 24 voices, PMON sources, shared Noise and reverb keep running. Off restores the original full mix and shared reverb. The short output fade retains the same song position; monitoring is independent of Live and does not change paused audition or Capture. Full audio and all 24 dry stems are retained only for the bounded lookahead, adding about 2 MiB of dry PCM with the default settings; only one selected AudioBuffer per segment is created. A compact row of 24 numbered CH buttons shows sampled Core active / ENV and selects the channel to inspect, audition or Capture. This is activity, not output level: silent modulators can still light. The underline shows ENV, amber when Gate is Off but the core remains active. Live Off, waiting and errors clear the indicators. Pause freezes the observed snapshot and activity buttons; choosing another channel reads that same state. Stop or Live Off restores the edited display. The read-only PCM canvas previews only the first 112 decoded samples at the programmed start address, not the current decoder output or a complete sample. Root tuning and software PMON parameters are not inferred. Pause the song with Live On, select CH1-24 and a Reference key (default C4), then choose Capture to Synth. View / keyboard selects Synth - edit and play or a PSF CH. Successful Capture keeps the song paused at the same position and channel and selects Synth for keyboard audition. Live remains enabled and the source CH activity stays visible, with no channel highlighted in Synth view. Resume continues the original song; choose any PSF CH, including the last channel number, to return to source observation or paused audition. Choosing a PSF CH enables Live if it was Off. Imported ADPCM from Capture, VAB Tone or a preset opens a full-sample PCM software editor on the same canvas, with a complete overview, zoom/range controls and indexed numeric or drag editing. Length, source loop boundaries, tuning, ADSR and effect settings are kept. Edits encode the complete PCM to ADPCM in a preparation Worker and stop held notes only when applying; ADPCM quantization changes the reconstructed waveform. Original bank bytes remain intact. Repeated edits reuse a private same-size SPU RAM slot; the first edit needs free RAM for that copy, and failed/cancelled preparation keeps the current sound. Saved instrument JSON retains the edited ADPCM. The 112-sample Morph checkbox is disabled for full samples rather than replacing their sound with default Sine. Choosing a shape explicitly creates a short editable cycle and enables its Morph controls. Live sample RAM remains read-only; this full editor never decodes the live song RAM. Continue editing in paused Synth view without stopping the song or losing the source CH snapshot. Supported channel controls and authored Synth-view edits keep playback running; loading another instrument retains its existing Stop behavior. The snapshot includes same-frame SPU RAM from a bounded private history, so later lookahead writes cannot replace the captured bytes. For ADPCM, original contiguous bytes, internal loop, ADSR, voice volume and playback Pitch are imported as a normal keyboard instrument. The Reference key reproduces the captured raw Pitch and does not identify a sample root. A new note starts its envelope afresh. Shared editor reverb is kept; song main volume and custom shared effects are not copied. PMON carriers (including Noise with PMON) are rejected before changing the edited sound. ADPCM also requires a valid END, contiguous non-wrapped loop and consistent markers. Noise captures copy shared Noise Clock, ADSR, voice levels and send, with a fixed 64-byte silent support loop instead of source ADPCM. Noise has no Reference key tuning: every keyboard key triggers the same Noise clock and a fresh envelope; running LFSR phase is not copied. Source PITCH, Start, Repeat and ADPCM contents do not define the captured Noise sound. Capture history uses about 3.5 MiB with the shipped lookahead (up to about 4 MiB including one paused image); advanced transport settings scale the bounded history with lookahead. Live Off stops RAM acquisition. Paused keyboard audition borrows the editor checkpoint without saving or replacing its instrument; use Capture to Synth for a permanent copy. Save to presets or Instrument SPU JSON retains the captured sample and tuning. Stop restores its samples and settings. This ZIP contains no BIOS, games, or recordings.

The live JavaScript and CSS are copied byte-for-byte from the authored modules, preserving comments, names and relative imports. They are not bundled or minified: edit the files in synth-spu/, js/, synth/ or playground/ and reload the served page without a JavaScript build step. The same frontend tree can be imported into a Tauri application; rebuild that application after changing its packaged assets. The keyboard Synth's pinned Emscripten factory and WASM are copied unchanged under generated/. The separate PSF player uses the documented ABI 5 monitor build. Native-generated loaders may retain their compact upstream formatting. Audio runtime dependencies are local. Monaco uses its pinned public CDN and falls back to the local textarea if unavailable. Navigation links open the full Tetorica website.

Original browser inputs and the packaging recipe are included in sources/spu-synth-browser-inputs.zip. sources/spu-synth-browser.json records each live module, its original source path, hash and local imports. SPU C++ source, upstream attribution, licenses, checksums, and a standalone rebuild recipe are included under sources/; see sources/PS1-SPU.md. See LICENSE and licenses/mame-ps1-spu/LICENSE for the respective BSD-3-Clause licenses. The separate PSF1 player includes readable Play!, Framework and CodeGen sources under sources/psf-player/ with BSD-2-Clause notices and provenance, together with the unchanged MAME SPU DSP sources under BSD-3-Clause and a standalone Emscripten rebuild recipe. See licenses/play-psf/ and licenses/mame-ps1-spu/LICENSE.
